title: The upper cell (p+1)^{2^r} forces enough top-window mass to exclude leftover L=84 at m≥3
statement: On a Juggler CycleMin of length 84 at residual floor 261, the even-run upper cell M < (p+1)^{2^r} together with the odd-run height of the peak forces a landing p ≥ iterated_isqrt(M_min, r) that, stacked on height packing, excludes every m≥3 under a proved finance constant.
counterexamples: 6/5 first kills at p≥659; inv-sum first kills at p≥367; the adversarial landing 304 is below both
Pigeonhole k=18 lands at p=3075 and would kill; a leftover m=3 word may use k=24. Large m is worse
mathematical_domain: Juggler cycle finance / top even-run cell
notes: The landing bound is a corollary of even_iter_lt_succ_pow plus monotone isqrt, not a new defect law. The leftover-killer reading is the only novel half and is false. Not a leftover-itinerary census, not a floor raise, and not a halt theorem.
tested_range: L=84, n=261, exact peak runs k=18..24, log2 lower bounds k=25..51, pigeonhole m=3..31; constants 1 and 6/5 and Lean inv-sum
